title: Coverage — statements, node order and time
summary: Coverage items: true/false statements across diagrams, ordering nodes with and without a time axis, lineage ages against dated fossils, and what a cladogram does not show.

items.text: Select every true statement. The node letters are on the first tree.

statements.text: The first and second trees show the same relationships.
A and B form a clade in the first tree but not in the third.
E and F form a clade in the first tree but not in the third.
The first and third trees show the same relationships.
Node R is older than node P.

items.text: Order the lettered nodes from oldest to youngest.
items.note_after: A node is older than every node below it. Nodes on separate lineages cannot be ordered against each other — every order consistent with ancestry is accepted.

items.text: Order the lettered nodes from oldest to youngest. The scale shows time in million years before today.
Select every true statement. The scale shows time in million years before today; node letters and ages are on the tree.

statements.text: The hippo lineage is at least 30 million years old — its split from the whales is at least that old.
The hippo lineage is at least 40 million years old.
Node W is older than 50 million years.
Node C is older than 50 million years.

options: No — it shows only branching order; it has no time component
Yes — the tips sit on a time axis
Yes — longer branches always mean more time

items.text: This tree leaves the branching order of the squirrel, the guinea pig and the mouse–rat pair unresolved — a three-way split. What does that mean?

options: The branching order is not resolved — the drawing cannot say which split came first
The three lineages really split in a single instant

items.text: A dendrogram drawn from overall similarity scores groups tips that look alike. What can a phylogenetic tree claim that such a dendrogram cannot?

options: It claims shared ancestry, not just similarity
Nothing — the two diagrams mean the same thing
It is always better at grouping by similarity

items.text: Suppose a tree of parasites drawn next to this tree of their hosts had almost the same shape. What would that suggest?

options: The parasites tended to speciate when their hosts did
The parasites spread between hosts at random
The hosts evolved to match their parasites
